Subject: Quick recap & procurement path question (no PO)

Hi Sophie / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the evaluation goals (reduce inference cost for clinical NLP, consistent latency across regions, and better observability for token spend). Per our notes, next steps are a short pilot (2 GPUs, 6 weeks) and a procurement check so we can get billing and legal lined up.

Two quick clarifying items from procurement that will determine the commercial path:
- You mentioned procurement is not issuing POs for third-party SaaS. Can you confirm that the only paths are corporate card payment or a marketplace (AWS/GCP marketplace) purchase?
- Is there any prepay requirement or minimum term that would block a standard month-to-month card charge?

I attached the short excerpt you shared on the call so we have it in the thread. If card/marketplace are the only options, we can propose a marketplace listing or a short prepay option — and I can loop in our finance ops to confirm the billing flow.

Attachments: procurement_policy_excerpt.txt (text excerpt provided during call)

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Confirm procurement path (card only vs marketplace + any prepay thresholds) — Sophie/Daniel
2) If card only, confirm PO exception request would be necessary — we can request an exception via nossa internal process
3) If marketplace required, indicate preferred marketplace (AWS or GCP) and we’ll prioritize integration

I’ll pull pricing options for both card and marketplace flows once we have confirmation.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Alex —

Confirming from my side: Medicore does not issue POs for SaaS vendors in most cases. The two routes we use are:
- AWS Marketplace (preferred for centralized cost allocation), or
- Corporate card for short pilots / limit under $10k.

If a vendor cannot be purchased via marketplace and the spend is expected > $10k, procurement will escalate to our vendor review (which typically requires SOW and a payment method confirmation). I’m looping Procurement directly — they’ll outline thresholds and any prepay requirements.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Head of Data & AI, Medicore Health
sophie@medicore.com
From: Procurement Team <procurement@medicore.com>

Cc: 
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap & procurement path question (no PO)

Hi Alex —

Procurement here. Short summary of our vendor policy relevant to this request:
- We do not issue traditional purchase orders for SaaS contracts with variable-month usage unless the vendor is onboarded to AWS Marketplace and supports consolidated billing.
- For card payments: small pilots (< $10k) can be handled via corporate card. Anything > $10k requires vendor onboarding and an approved commercial path.
- We sometimes require a short prepay (1–2 months) when vendor onboarding cannot be completed before pilot start; this is assessed case-by-case.
- Spend thresholds: onboarding review triggers at $25k ARR expectation or a contract longer than 6 months.

If Redwood can provide either: a marketplace listing (AWS or GCP) with consolidated billing, or accept a 2-month prepay while we complete onboarding, we can move faster. Otherwise we’ll need to initiate our vendor review which can add ~3–4 weeks.

Please provide a short options list for (a) card-only pilot, (b) marketplace purchase, (c) prepay proposal. We prefer concise bullets with estimated $s and any contract terms.

Thanks,
Medicore Procurement
procurement@medicore.com
Attachments referenced: ProcurementPolicy_v3.pdf
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Procurement confirmation — need to decide exception vs marketplace priority

Marissa / Sean —

Forwarding Medicore’s procurement reply. Key constraints: no PO, prefers AWS Marketplace or corporate card for pilots; onboarding review at $25k and prepay sometimes required. Pilot window is tight (they want to start in 2–3 weeks).

Can we do any of the following quickly?
1) Fast-track an AWS Marketplace listing for a pilot SKU (short lead times are hard, but is there a reseller workaround?)
2) Offer a 2-month prepay pilot invoice (we take prepay; finance ops sign-off needed) — provide pricing for 2 months of the pilot (estimate attached)
3) Approve a procurement exception template (we’ve used this before for card-only exceptions) — what approvals do we need and how long?

Attachments: RDW_pricing_options_Medicore.xlsx (pricing estimates), deal_notes_Medicore.txt

They’re also explicitly asking for concise bullets with estimated $s. I can draft that, but want to align on naming and whether we can accept prepay without lengthly legal/finance delays.

Appreciate a quick take — they want to start early April.

Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement confirmation — need to decide exception vs marketplace priority

Alex / Sean —

Suggested path to keep Medicore in-window for an early-April start: follow option (2) + parallel exception request. Details below.

Option A — 2-month prepay pilot (fastest)- Proposal: 2 months prepaid at 50% of list for the pilot configuration (2x A100-equiv GPU, up to 5M tokens/month).
- Invoice terms: immediate payment by corporate card or wire; Redwood issues standard MSA (no PO required).
- Pros: immediate start, finance ops can process prepay as cash receipt.
- Cons: Procurement will still want vendor onboarding; they may ask for a refund/credit mechanism if onboarding later enables marketplace billing.

Option B — Marketplace reseller workaround (medium)- We can use a verified reseller to place the SKU on their AWS Marketplace account and consolidate billing to Medicore. Lead time ~2–3 weeks depending on reseller onboarding.
- Pros: satisfies their centralized billing requirement.
- Cons: still requires reseller setup and Marketplace listing work.

Option C — Procurement exception (slowest)- Use exception_request_template.docx (attached) to request a limited card-only exception for the pilot. Approval required from Finance Ops and Legal; expect 5–10 business days.

Recommended immediate action:
1) Offer the 2-month prepay pilot price below (we can price at $24,000 prepaid for the two-month pilot; details in RDW_pricing_options_Medicore.xlsx).
2) Simultaneously open procurement exception with the attached template so they have an alternate path if prepay is unacceptable.
3) If Medicore confirms AWS Marketplace is strictly required, escalate to Partner Ops to engage reseller program (Sean to own).

I’ll prepare the concise bullets to send back to Medicore. Alex — if you want, I’ll draft the pricing bullets now and you can send.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
